newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW -Japan June industrial production.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -Japan June industrial production.

text.p: Below are analysts' intitial reactions to Japan's June industrial production data.

The Trade Ministry on Wednesday said June industrial output fell a preliminary 3.1 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis. The ministry forecast a 1.3 percent month-on-month rise for July but a 0.5 percent drop for August.
YO OGIWARA, BOND RESEARCH, NOMURA SECURITIES INVESTMENT TRUST:

"The 3.1 percent drop is within our expectations. The bond market has already discounted this data, so it will probably have a very limited impact on the market. It looks like in the July-September (period) recovery still continues, but it will be a very slow recovery. My forecast is that the Japanese economy is slowing down and Japanese interest rates will go down. I don't think there will be any change in the BOJ's monetary policy ahead."
YASUNARI UENO, CHIEF MARKET ECONOMIST, FUJI SECURITIES CO:

"The June figures were basically within expectations. We predicted about 3.5 percent ourselves. JGBs were bought a bit just after the numbers came out simply because it was a fall to the three percent range, but because there'd been talk in the market this morning that the fall could be as much as four percent, the figures were partially factored in, limiting the impact."
"JGBs were bought quite a bit in the morning, and these figures are not really enough to push them up even further for now. Expect them to drift roughly at current levels."
"Considering the July and August figures, neither is really enough to suggest definitely that the economy will be getting much stronger, limiting their negative impact on JGBs."

"I think the foreign exchange market is discounting the sluggish period in the current quarter. But I do think it's going to be mildly a dollar positive. We are going to continue to see the dollar-yen gradually move higher. They (market operators) continue to hold the view the BOJ is not going to tighten monetary policy in the near future. (They think the BOJ will tighten monetary policy) probably late this year or more likely early next year. The fact is that the yield differentials are going to remain wide for quite a while, and that's going to support the dollar.
